chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Describing Tatum's technique and touch
summary: Ramirez struggles to describe how Tatum repeated one note with four fingers and his intuitive blind sensitivity.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, he wasn't himself a... He was a schooled pianist, but he wasn't a great pianist himself.
Was he? I never heard him play.
No. He was a good piano player, but not a...
Well, he was more a composer, wasn't he.
And he could appreciate what Tatum was doing.
Well, no one could describe... I'm doing a very poor thing describing what Tatum could do.

No one could describe just how these things happened with this man... To watch Tatum, the way he... He would say like a name. He would hit one key, and he could hit it with all four fingers and repeat it...

Well, he substituted his fingering. And of course, it looked awkward, because to me, sometimes you couldn't see what he was doing. I think due to his feeling, the way he felt... You know, people that don't use their eyes and blind like that, they have a certain tonal sensitivity...
